identifier: Y. J. Lee, J. D. Park, "Microscopic origins of second normal stress difference in a colloidal gel under startup shear", Physics of Fluids 38, 023308 (2026). DOI 10.1063/5.0314634. Values entered come from Sec. II B (simulation details) and Sec. III text.
delivered_by: the person, as the publisher's PDF in ~/Downloads on the MacBook, named in task 039. Nineteen pages; no supplementary material is referred to.
publication_status: PEER REVIEWED, CHECKED ON THE FILE. Typeset version of record: submitted 30 November 2025, accepted 19 January 2026, published online 4 February 2026.
grade_rule: E3, grade_tag peer_reviewed. Every result is a claim about the MODEL: Brownian dynamics of Morse-attractive spheres with far-field (Rotne-Prager-Yamakawa) hydrodynamics and no lubrication, gelled and then sheared.
license_note: Published under an exclusive licence by AIP Publishing; NOT open access. Identifier, stated conditions and numbers only; nothing of the text or figures is reproduced.
method_as_stated: Brownian dynamics in the overdamped limit with many-body far-field hydrodynamics through the RPY mobility tensor (inertia, an explicit fluid field and non-Newtonian solvent all absent); lubrication deliberately left out. The Brownian displacement uses the Positively Split Ewald method of Fiore et al., through the authors' latest HOOMD-blue plugin, run under HOOMD 2.4.0 with CUDA 9.2 on an Intel Xeon Gold 6226R with an NVIDIA GeForce GTX 1070, at about 1,500 time steps per hour. The authors warn that the plugin has compatibility problems across HOOMD releases and fails unmodified, note that the current release when they wrote was 5.4.0, and point to a Python Stokesian-dynamics implementation with RPY mobility for reproducibility. INTERACTION: Morse potential of depth V0 = 15 kT, width parameter kappa a = 30, cut off at 3.0 (particle radius a = 1); the stress is computed from the interparticle forces alone (RPY here carries no stresslets); neighbours within r/a of about 2.113. UNITS: length a, energy kT, time 6 pi eta a^3/kT. GELATION: 10,648 particles placed at random in a cubic box at volume fraction 0.2, time step 1e-4 until 100 time units; the resulting gel has mean coordination 6.136 and mean bond number 2.014 and is rigid without being at an energy minimum. SHEAR: time step 1e-6; shear Peclet number Pe = 6 pi eta gammadot a^3/kT from 15 to 300, equivalently Mason number Mn = 6 pi eta gammadot a^3/V0 from 1 to 20, with Pe = 15 Mn.
not_entered: The stress-strain curves, number-weighted stress distributions and bond-angle statistics: figure-only (Figs. 2-9). The phenomenological potential-energy metric's accuracy (over by 30% at Pe 15, near-quantitative at Pe 50, under by 20% at Pe 300): a statement about the authors' own fitting device rather than about the model's physics; it is in the note. Normal-stress noise and system-size remarks citing other work: not this paper's result.
note: The software fact here is the one this repository most needs to know before reusing the recipe: the hydrodynamic plugin was run on HOOMD 2.4.0, and this repository pins HOOMD 7.2.0. Nothing in the source says whether the plugin can run on a 7.x release, and no entry asserts that it can.
